Combat Maneuvers

Combat Maneuvers

Combat Maneuvers are the universal combat options available to all player characters and NPCs.

They do not need to be learned, purchased, or gained through a Power.

Every combatant knows how to:

  • move,
  • make a Basic Attack,
  • and use Basic Reactions.

Powers expand, improve, or replace these basic options, but they are never required for a creature to participate effectively in combat.

This means that even if a character has no suitable Power available, has already used their Powers, or has not purchased additional combat Powers, they still have meaningful Movement, Attack, and Reaction options.

Every character normally has:

  • 1 Movement
  • 1 Attack Action
  • 1 Reaction

per round, unless another rule grants additional uses.

Additional Movements, Attack Actions, and Reactions may be gained through Stones, Powers, or other explicit effects.

Basic Combat Maneuvers are not Powers. They do not become spent after use. If a character gains additional uses of the appropriate action type, the same Basic Combat Maneuver may be used again.

Basic Attack

Every character can make a normal attack without using an Active Power.

This is called a Basic Attack.

Damage

A Basic Attack deals:

Weapon Damage + MR × 2d8 Damage

Apply any eligible Passive, Active Buff, Artifact, weapon, or other effects that normally modify the attack or its damage.

Basic Attack Rules

No Power Required: A Basic Attack does not require an Active Power.

No Power Effects: You may not add damage, Specials, AoE, Split Attack, Autofire, control effects, or other effects belonging to an Active Power unless another rule explicitly allows it.

Weapon Properties Apply: Normal properties and effects belonging to the weapon itself still apply when appropriate.

Extra Attacks: If you gain additional Attack Actions through Stones, Powers, or another effect, you may use them to make additional Basic Attacks.

A Basic Attack is not a Power and does not become spent after use.

Threatened Ranged Attacks

When you declare a Ranged Attack or Ranged Power using a bow, crossbow, thrown weapon, or similar ranged weapon while you are within an enemy's Melee Reach, the attack is Threatened.

Make this Ranged Attack with Disadvantage.

Threatened Spellcasting: Declare a legal Spell Casting Roll while within an enemy's Melee Reach: the Casting Roll has Disadvantage. This applies regardless of the Spell's effect or eligible delivery: damage, healing (including self-healing), Cleanse, Restoration, support, control, AoE, persistent zones, and any otherwise permitted melee- or touch-range Spell. The restriction applies to the Casting Roll, not to subsequent Damage or Healing Dice. It does not forbid casting, alter Spell TNs, or permit otherwise illegal Spell delivery.

Determine the threat when the Attack or Spell is declared, using the enemy's actual Melee Reach. Several threatening enemies still impose one Disadvantage, not additional stacking penalties. A persistent Spell effect does not make a new Casting Roll or receive a new threatened check merely because it ticks or affects a new creature.

After declaration, each enemy whose Melee Reach includes you may use an available legal Reaction if its printed trigger and other requirements are satisfied. Threatened status creates no new Reaction type, waives no requirements, and does not change the normal rules for Reactions on Reactions. Normal Melee Martial Attacks do not gain this Disadvantage merely for being within reach.

Movement

Every character can move without purchasing a Movement Power.

Your normal Movement represents basic tactical positioning during your Turn.

Threat Zone Movement Triggers

A creature crossing the boundary of an enemy's Threat Zone triggers that enemy's eligible movement Reaction once per crossing, whether entering or leaving. Resolve an entry trigger after the step into the Zone, and an exit trigger immediately before the step out. The moving creature is inside the Zone when the Reaction resolves. Safe Movement and Disengage suppress movement-triggered Reactions for their protected movement.

Normal Movement

Move Distance: Move up to your Speed in meters.

Draw / Sheathe: You may draw or sheathe a weapon as part of your Movement.

No Splitting: If you use a Movement Maneuver or Movement Power that replaces your Movement, it uses that entire Movement and cannot be split unless a rule explicitly says otherwise.

Movement Powers provide additional or superior movement options such as Teleport, Flight, Leap, Safe Movement, or other specialized movement.

They are not required to move normally.

Basic Movement Options

Choose one option whenever you use a normal Movement, unless another rule says otherwise.

Move

Move up to your Speed.

This movement provokes movement-triggered Reactions normally.

Dash

Focus entirely on movement.

Move up to double your normal Speed.

This requires an available base Attack Action to forfeit for this Turn. If it was already spent or committed to an Active Buff during Preparation, you cannot Dash. Legal additional Attack Actions remain usable, but cannot pay this base-Action forfeit.

This movement provokes movement-triggered Reactions normally.

Disengage

Withdraw carefully.

Move up to your normal Speed without provoking movement-triggered Reactions.

This requires an available base Attack Action to forfeit for this Turn. If it was already spent or committed to an Active Buff during Preparation, you cannot Disengage. Legal additional Attack Actions remain usable, but cannot pay this base-Action forfeit.

Quick Load

Convert Movement into reloading.

Instead of moving, spend your Movement to perform Reload (1).

If you gain additional Movements, you may use Quick Load multiple times during the same Turn, up to a maximum total Reload equal to your Mastery Rank.

You still need one free hand and must be able to manipulate the weapon or ammunition.

You cannot use Quick Load while you cannot legally spend Movement.

Stand Up

Recover from Prone by spending 1 Attack Action. Until you stand, your normal Evade and passive defenses apply, but you cannot move, attack, cast or use Reactions. After standing, your Movement and other available actions function normally.

Standing up itself does not provoke Reactions. Movement taken afterward may provoke normally.

Basic Attack Actions

Every character can use Basic Attack Actions without purchasing an Active Power.

Using a Basic Attack Action spends 1 Attack Action.

Basic Attack Actions are not Powers and do not become spent after use.

Basic Attack

Requirement: A Weapon or Natural Weapon capable of making the Attack.

Effect: Make a normal Attack.

On hit, deal:

Weapon Damage + MR × 2d8 Damage

Eligible Passive, Active Buff, Artifact, weapon, and other effects apply normally.

A Basic Attack cannot add damage, Specials, AoE, Split Attack, Autofire, control effects, or other effects belonging to an Active Power unless another rule explicitly allows it.

If you gain additional Attack Actions, you may use them to make additional Basic Attacks.

Basic Reactions

Every character can use Basic Reactions without purchasing a Reaction Power.

Using a Basic Reaction spends 1 Reaction.

Basic Reactions are not Powers and do not become spent after use.

If a character gains additional Reactions through Stones, Powers, or another effect, they may use Basic Reactions again whenever their Trigger occurs.

Reaction Powers provide stronger, more specialized, or more tactical responses, but they are not required to react in combat.

Guard

Trigger: You are hit by an Attack or would take damage.

Effect: Gain +MR × 2 Armor against the triggering Attack or damage instance.

This Armor is added to your existing Armor and applies only against the triggering event.

Evade

Trigger: An Attack is declared against you, before its Attack Roll or Casting Roll.

Effect: Gain +MR × 2 Evade against the triggering Attack.

This Evade is added to your existing Evade and applies only against the triggering Attack.

Dive for Cover

Trigger: You would be hit by an AoE Attack after its shared Attack Roll or Casting Roll has been compared to your defense, but before its damage or payload is applied.

Effect: Immediately move up to 2 × Mastery Rank meters.

If this movement takes you completely outside the AoE, you are not affected by that AoE.

If you remain inside the area, you are affected normally.

This movement does not provoke movement-triggered Reactions.

Dive for Cover is available to any creature that would be hit by the AoE, including a creature standing at its center point. If you already spent your Reaction on Reaction: Evade, you need another available Reaction to also use Dive for Cover.

Escape Rule: Flee

To use Flee, spend 1 Movement and 1 Attack Action on your Turn. Both must still be available when you declare Flee. Move up to 4 × your normal Speed directly away from danger as that Flee action.

Until the start of your next Turn:

  • you cannot make Attacks,
  • you cannot use Reactions,
  • and you cannot spend Stones.

This movement provokes movement-triggered Reactions normally.

Pursuit

When a creature uses Flee and another creature continues pursuing it, the GM may begin a Pursuit.

A Pursuit is resolved through repeated Opposed Attribute Contests.

For each exchange, both creatures use the physical Attribute that best fits how they are trying to gain ground. Agility is common for speed and maneuvering, Might for forcing through obstacles or overpowering resistance, and Vitality for an exchange defined by endurance. The GM may restrict the choice when the situation clearly favors one approach.

Track the Pursuit from 0.

  • If the fleeing creature wins a Contest, move the Pursuit +1.
  • If the pursuing creature wins a Contest, move the Pursuit −1.
  • A tie causes no change.

At +2, the fleeing creature escapes completely.

At −2, the pursuer catches the fleeing creature and the Pursuit ends.

Each Contest represents one meaningful exchange of the chase, such as sprinting through streets, vaulting obstacles, climbing, cutting through crowds, or gaining ground.

Normal situational rules such as Advantage, Disadvantage, terrain, movement modes, and relevant circumstances may apply.

Healing Sources at a Glance

Source Recovery Resource
Resolve: Healing Rolled HP in the active Bar Prepaid Stone application, used during the current Round
Damage Transfer HP equal to real HP lost by its target Its successful damage instance
Restoration Actives Fully refilled Scarred Bars on eligible recipients Power-specific pool per Safe Haven Rest
Passive: Regeneration Fully refilled Scarred Bars on Self Limited pool per Tyhran Day
Vitality: Remove Scar Fully refilled Scarred Bars on Self Sealed Vitality Stones, Rank limits
Natural / Safe Haven Recovery Printed active-Bar HP and Scarred-Bar recovery Time and rest conditions
